nodes.title: MAB-Seq
nodes.scope: Illumina explanatory core MAB-seq schematic, including its upper untreated bisulfite control and lower M.SssI branch. MAB-seq is M.SssI methylase-assisted bisulfite sequencing. The five icons represent cytosine modification classes at corresponding positions, not a literal five-base genomic sequence. The target is DNA-borne 5fC plus 5caC; the final carrier is amplified DNA encoding their combined signal as T. Library construction internals are not drawn. A separate primary-paper extension records the locus-specific caMAB-seq implementation explicitly mentioned by the catalogue: M.SssI, then selective 5fC reduction, then bisulfite/PCR. Its extra route is not depicted in the Illumina image and is not merged with the MAB-seq route. RRMAB-seq is recognized only at the related abstract evidence level; applicability of individual diagram operations and its unshown representation-selection front end are not resolved here.

original.description: Convert bisulfite-susceptible bases in untreated DNA and amplify the converted template, yielding the depicted T-C-C-T-T product.

original.label: Bisulfite treatment; PCR amplification (M.SssI branch)
original.description: Convert the methylase-protected DNA and amplify the converted template, yielding the depicted C-C-C-T-T product.
original.mechanism: Originally unmodified CpG C is protected as 5mC; 5fC and 5caC remain bisulfite susceptible and produce T-coded positions after PCR. Original 5mC and 5hmC produce C-coded positions.
original.information_effect: At CpGs, the physical carrier is amplified DNA and its T calls provide a direct combined 5fC/5caC signal at corresponding genomic positions.
